name: FlashBlade - quarantine client (day 2)
description: An operator asks for an NFS client to be made read-only on the file systems it is exported to, or released again. A human approves it, the export entry or export policy rule is rewritten through the FlashBlade REST API and the outcome is logged with the AAP job link. Never a block: the client keeps reading. A rejection is logged and changes nothing.

client.title: Client address
client.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address of the NFS client, as the array reports it

file_system.title: File system
file_system.description: One file system name, or empty for every live file system whose NFS export names the client

action.title: Action
action.description: quarantine makes the client read-only, release gives it back what it had

parameters.prompt: ${trigger.action} client ${trigger.client} on ${trigger.array} (file system: ${trigger.file_system}; empty means every live file system whose export names the client). A quarantine rewrites the client's export entry rw -> ro, or inserts a read-only export policy rule for it; a release reverses that. Never a block: the client keeps reading. Addresses in contain_exclude_clients, the array's own interfaces and its replication peers are refused; file systems matching contain_exclude_file_systems are left alone.

extra_vars.reason: requested through the orchestrator (FlashBlade - quarantine client (day 2))

extra_vars.subject: Client ${trigger.client} on ${trigger.array}: ${trigger.action} changed ${quarantine_client.artifacts.changed_count} file system(s)
extra_vars.detail: File systems: ${quarantine_client.artifacts.file_systems}. The quarantine record in the alert log carries every export before and after, and any refusal. AAP job: ${quarantine_client.job_url}

extra_vars.subject: ${trigger.action} of client ${trigger.client} on ${trigger.array} rejected or expired; nothing changed
extra_vars.detail: The approval was rejected or timed out after 24 hours. Raise a new request if the ${trigger.action} is still wanted.
